where: module/rules/kinds/bonus.mjs, the Defense branch of a check; ruling 222 (0.21.0)
question: Ruling 222 lets a bonus to a Maneuver reach a check rolled with a Defense Constellation from that Maneuver's Item (Humanity's +1 on an Aid made with Awareness). Should a bonus to every check, and a bonus to a Maneuver made without its Item, also reach a Defense rolled as a check (Wind's Endure, a Recovery, a Search with Awareness)? Today neither does: nothing is applied and nothing is offered there.
recommendation: Yes, as its own ruling, with a Wind roll driven live, because it changes numbers outside Aid.

where: module/rules/kinds/substitute.mjs, the third descriptor of USE; rulings 219 and 111
question: A USE line names a Maneuver's check and nothing wider (ruling 219); a Constellation there is refused ('a Constellation's own checks are not read yet'). When a Talent wants a Constellation as the check a USE names, does the swap carry into an Initiative rolled with that Constellation? Ruling 111 (an Initiative rolled with a Constellation carries every modifier of that Constellation's check) argues yes.
recommendation: Settle it with the first Talent that names one; the refusal stands until then.

where: data/ancestries.xlsx, the Human sheet in progress (Mike's, uncommitted)
question: 16 Automation cells on the Human sheet hold only '# PROPOSED' notes naming tags the grammar does not have (ALTER, PREPARE, CONDITION and extra IF conditions), Jack of All Trades' and Quick Study's among them, so those Talents automate nothing once the sheet builds; and Torchbearer Human's cell no longer carries the Rally Aura. Which comes first?
recommendation: Pick the next kind from them with Claude, one at a time (ruling 119), from the Talent that wants it most; the others stay '#' notes, which the grammar reads as comments, until their kind exists. Cells that can be written today are printed in the 0.22.0, 0.24.0 and 0.25.0 changelog entries and in AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5. Four are already on the saved sheets (Patient Assistance, Sure Assistance, Coordinated Footwork, Move Together's row). Three things wait: Aid's five GIVE lines on its row (0.22.0; its Automation cell is still empty, so no Aid gives a result), a ROW for Pay It Forward on the Ancestry Actions sheet (Cost 0, Frequency 'Once per encounter', text from the draft workbook) with '[EFFECT SUBORDINATE: Aid; IF: EFFECT(Aid, used); LIMIT: encounter]', and '[EFFECT ALTER: Pay It Forward.limit; VALUE: round]' on Reciprocal Effort (0.25.0).

where: PHB v4.25, Conditions table (a tracked change); data/maneuvers.xlsx, Drop Prone, Stand, Kip Up and a Roll Over row to come
question: Mike's Supine rules are in the handbook's Conditions table as a tracked change (Off-Guard; -2 Situation to Attacks except melee against an adjacent creature; +2 Situation to Evade against ranged; no Move, Step, Rush, Leap or Crawl; Stand or Roll Over to clear), with one sentence of Claude's as its own insertion ("Supine is not Prone: a rule that names one does not mean the other"). The system still has Prone alone (ruling 266).
recommendation: Accept or edit the cell in Word, add the Roll Over row (Cost 1, Traits Motion, Requirements "You are Prone or Supine.", Effect "Change from Prone to Supine, or from Supine to Prone.") and enable Drop Prone on the Basic Actions sheet, then have Supine built: a condition beside Prone, the attack penalty read against the gap to the target, the movement refusal in the drag, and Roll Over as a Maneuver the system implements.

where: World setting "Track the six-action round" (trackActions)
question: The setting has only ever switched off the spending for movement, and since 0.23.0 for a Maneuver used from the sheet (ruling 236). Strikes, Casts, Reactions, Raise a Shield, Recenter and drawing or stowing a weapon are paid whether it is on or off, although its hint said otherwise until 0.23.0. Should Off stop those as well?
recommendation: Leave it as it is. A Strike or a Cast is declared through the attack flow, which refunds on Cancel and reads the pool, so an unpaid Strike would be a second path to keep right; a table that wants no counting can ignore the pips, which nothing enforces.

where: data/maneuvers.xlsx Athletics Actions, Grapple
question: Grapple prints a cost of nought with an Athletics check against Evade, so since 0.23.0 it is the one Maneuver that rolls an attack-like check and pays nothing. Shove, Trip and Reposition beside it cost one or two.
recommendation: Read as a slip: give Grapple the cost the book prints for it, and the row pays it the next time the content builds.

where: data/maneuvers.xlsx Cost cells: Battle Cry, Lost in the Dark, Reliable Anchor, Steady the Line, Sure Seat, Quick Tongue, No Quarter, Grab an Edge
question: These rows have a Trigger and no Reaction glyph in their Cost, so the system reads each as a plain Maneuver. Since 0.23.0 a plain Maneuver used from the sheet pays its cost, so the five that cost one action pay it from their row and wait for the GM off-turn (Quick Tongue pays from its card button; the two at nought pay nothing). The same is true of any row whose empty Cost cell reads as one action.
recommendation: Write the cost with its Reaction glyph in each Cost cell (Battle Cry is nought with the glyph in the book). A Reaction is paid the moment it is used and never waits for the GM.

where: foundry/starwrought/module/documents/item.mjs, the Reaction branch of a Maneuver's use
question: A row printed with a cost and a Reaction half of its own, as Aid once was (one action, with a free Reaction), pays the Reaction half whenever it is used and never the printed cost. No shipped row is written so today.
recommendation: If such a row returns: used at your own Opportunity it is the Maneuver and pays the printed cost; used at any other time it is the Reaction and pays the half. Say the word and it is a small change.

where: module/rules/effects.mjs, the EFFECT condition; module/rules/given.mjs, the used Effect (0.25.0, ruling 247)
question: Named Effects were built in two steps by Mike's choice. Step one ships: the system leaves 'Aid from Wren (used)' when a roll uses a bonus up, and IF: EFFECT(Aid, used) reads it. Step two is his Fantasy Grounds idea in full: a Maneuver puts a named Effect on its target for a duration, and CHECK, DEF and ATK lines apply IF: EFFECT(<name>) on the owner or IFT: EFFECT(<name>) on the other party.
recommendation: Plan it on its own when the first row wants it (Unbroken Courage and Rallying Word's options are candidates). It needs a tag for granting an Effect, a writer for another player's character (the Give relay is the model) and a decision on whether Oathbound's MARK folds into it.

where: Chapter 4 of the handbook, beside 'A Strike made as part of another Maneuver'; ruling 245 (0.25.0)
question: The Subordinate Maneuver rule is Mike's and the system runs on it since 0.25.0: a Maneuver performed as part of another is done at the first Maneuver's listed cost and costs no additional actions, unless otherwise specified. The handbook has no sentence for it.
recommendation: Have Claude leave it as one tracked-change sentence against the current edition, for Mike to accept or reject, once v4.25 is synced.
decidedBy: ruling 265 (0.26.0): a tracked change in Chapter 8's Maneuvers paragraph of v4.25 itself, Mike's choice of place

where: data/magic.xlsx (the Targets column is prose); module/canvas/area-targets.mjs; PHB v4.25, Area Attacks
question: 0.26.0 aims an area and rules none of it: a template you draw targets what is inside, and the attack rolls once for each target. The book's own clauses wait for data: "Unless the Talent specifies otherwise" (no Talent can ask for one roll for all), a spell's own shape and size, and "an area Attack does not automatically gain these location-specific effects" (the system cannot tell an area Attack from another, so its Critical Hit effect is the GM's to switch off).
recommendation: Plan it on its own when the first area spell is authored: two columns on the spell rows (Area: shape and size; Rolls: each or one), the Cast placing the template and removing it when the attack ends, and the Critical Hit effect withheld for an attack that came from one.

where: v4.25-sync-report.md, rulings 256 and 260
question: Two readings the sync made that the book does not settle. 256: two overlapping Difficult regions of the SAME kind are two effects (x3), as two of different kinds are. 260: every Critical Hit that does damage sets its Zone's effect, an area Attack's included, and the Zone's switch on the sheet is the GM's remedy.
recommendation: Leave both unless play says otherwise; 256 is the one most likely to be argued (one circumstance counted once would make two mud regions x2).
